guides.title: Navigating the Linux Desktop & Basic Shell Commands
guides.symptom: New to Linux and don't know how to navigate folders, launch programs, or use the terminal
guides.description: Learn the fundamentals of Linux desktop environments (GNOME, KDE), file system hierarchy (/home, /etc, /var), and essential shell commands.
causes: Unfamiliarity with root filesystem layout (/ vs C:\ in Windows)
Not knowing fundamental shell navigation commands
guides.whyItWorks: In Linux, everything is treated as a file under a single root directory (`/`). Your personal documents live in `/home/username/`. Knowing `pwd`, `ls`, and `cd` gives you universal navigation power across all Linux distributions.

steps.detail: On almost all Linux desktops (Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian, Mint), press Ctrl + Alt + T to instantly launch the terminal emulator window.

steps.instruction: Navigate directories with basic shell commands
steps.detail:
Type these foundational commands:
- `pwd` — Print working directory (shows where you are)
- `ls -lah` — List all files including hidden ones with sizes
- `cd Documents` — Enter the Documents folder
- `cd ..` — Move up one directory level
- `cd ~` — Immediately return to your home directory

Standard commands run safely with your user account. When modifying system files or installing packages, prefix the command with `sudo` (SuperUser DO). For example: `sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager`. You will be asked for your login password (keystrokes will remain invisible for security).

guides.title: Installing and Removing Software on Linux (APT, DNF, Snap, Flatpak)
guides.symptom: I don't know how to install or uninstall applications on my Linux distribution
guides.description: Master package management across major distributions: Ubuntu/Debian (`apt`), Fedora/RHEL (`dnf`), Arch (`pacman`), and universal Flatpaks.
causes: Different Linux distros use distinct native package managers
Outdated local package index caches causing 'Unable to locate package' errors
guides.whyItWorks: Linux uses centralized cryptographically-verified repositories. Running `update` synchronizes repository metadata, while `install` automatically resolves, downloads, and compiles all shared library dependencies.

steps.detail:
First, update your local repository index list:
sudo apt update
To install an application (e.g., VLC):
sudo apt install vlc -y
To remove an application and its configuration files:
sudo apt purge vlc && sudo apt autoremove -y

To search, install, or remove packages:
sudo dnf check-update
sudo dnf install package_name -y
sudo dnf remove package_name -y

For software not in traditional repos, install via Flatpak (Flathub):
flatpak install flathub com.spotify.Client
Or via Snap on Ubuntu:
sudo snap install code --classic

guides.title: Fixing 'Permission Denied' Errors (chmod, chown, & sudo)
guides.symptom: Command fails with 'Permission denied' or unable to write/edit a file or script
guides.description: Understand Linux read/write/execute permissions (rwx) and fix ownership of user files locked by root.
causes: Files created by `sudo` inside the user's home folder owned by root
Downloaded script missing the executable (+x) permission flag
guides.whyItWorks: Every Linux file has an owner, a group, and permission bits for Read (4), Write (2), and Execute (1). Setting correct ownership (`chown`) and adding execute rights (`chmod +x`) restores normal access without risking system security.

steps.detail:
If you downloaded a `.sh` or AppImage script and it won't run, add the execute flag in terminal:
chmod +x scriptname.sh
Then run it with:
./scriptname.sh

steps.instruction: Reclaim ownership of files locked by root (`chown`)
steps.detail:
If a folder in your home directory was accidentally created with `sudo` and you cannot edit it, run:
sudo chown -R $USER:$USER ~/target_folder
`$USER` automatically substitutes your current username.
